question: What happens during the process of transcription in cells?

options.text: DNA is replicated into identical copies
Proteins are folded into functional shapes

solution:
The correct answer is __**DNA is converted into RNA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Transcription** is the biological process where the **DNA sequence of a gene is copied into RNA**. It is the first step in gene expression.
 
• The enzyme **RNA polymerase** plays a central role in this process by binding to the DNA at the promoter region and synthesizing a complementary strand of RNA.
 
• In transcription, the DNA strand used as a template is called the **template strand**, while the complementary strand is referred to as the **coding strand**.
 
• The result of transcription is a single-stranded RNA molecule that is complementary to the DNA template strand. This RNA can be **messenger RNA (mRNA)**, **ribosomal RNA (rRNA)**, or **transfer RNA (tRNA)**, depending on the gene being transcribed.
 
• Transcription occurs in the nucleus
